children: Egypt’s state-owned Banque du Caire will price its IPO at EGP 5.30 per share, the top of its indicative range, valuing the lender at EGP 80.8 billion at listing, two investment bankers with knowledge of the transaction told Zawya.
An official announcement on the pricing is expected tomorrow, with trading on the Egyptian Exchange expected to begin in November.

The offering, which was increased to 45% from an initial 30% following strong investor demand, comprises 6.86 billion shares and is expected to generate EGP 36.4 billion in proceeds for state-owned Banque Misr, the selling shareholder.
The final price compares with an indicative range of EGP 4.82–5.30 per share.
Institutional investors have been allocated 95% of the offering, with the remaining 5% reserved for retail investors.

The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and International Finance Corporation (IFC) have each agreed to subscribe for up to 15.74% of the enlarged private placement, subject to final allocations.
Banque Misr will retain a 55% stake following the offering.
(Reporting by Ahmad Mousa; editing by Seban Scaria)

title: Banque du Caire IPO set to price at top of range at EGP 5.30 per share
